discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 041742
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1242 PM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Rain tapering off by afternoon. Plenty of clouds around. 

- Not as warm today but remaining somewhat breezy with wind
  gusts of 25 to 30 mph. 

- Drying out tonight through Thursday morning before lake
  enhanced showers begin and persist into Saturday morning.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 1113 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Greater coverage of rain/rainshowers is slowly pushing east and
should exit the area near/after 18Z. behind this, isolated to
scattered shower or areas of drizzle persist ahead of the
initial trough that should bring an end to the majority of the
precip until Thursday when the stronger front arrives. Have
adjusted pops to reflect these trends, but otherwise no big
changes.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 214 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

A 1002mb low swirls over far southwest WI early this morning 
while a lagging cold front bulges into western IL. An area of 
rain is lifting through the Ohio River Valley beneath 75-knot 
500mb flow and a 50-knot 850-mb jet. Rain today will generally 
amount to 0.10- 0.25". Far northwest OH might see slightly 
more based on the trajectory of the heaviest returns upstream, 
in an area of favorable moisture convergence aided by the 
aformentioned jets. Forecast soundings show little chance of 
any deep low-level mixing today which will keep wind gusts in 
check; primarily 20 mph to 30 mph. Rain tapers off from west to 
east by early afternoon as the dryslot moves overhead. Cold air 
advection is delayed until late in the day due to boundary- 
parallel flow and will be most noticeable by Thursday when with 
lows in the mid- 40s and highs shy of 60 degrees (a touch mild 
still for early November). 

After a dry start to Thursday, a secondary trough axis ripples 
through in the late afternoon providing ample lift for scattered 
showers. Reinforcing cold air (2C at 850mb) over a 10-13C Lake 
Michigan results in lake enhanced showers that persist into 
Saturday morning. (If the airmass were colder, this would be a
solid LES setup.) Friday and Saturday are the coldest of this 
forecast period as deep troughing is entrenched over the eastern
Great Lakes. 

Temperatures inch upward early next week as we lie on the cusp of a 
south-central US ridge. How far east this ridge propagates is 
uncertain  with the prospect of a potential blocking pattern taking 
shape over the interior Rockies. For now, precipitation chances 
appear minimal, but a shift in energetic northwest flow could flip 
the script if the ridge is not as strong, bringing passing chances 
for light rain.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1235 PM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Initial trough is approaching KSBN with wind shift to SW
occurring near/just after valid time with the shift occurring a
few hours later at KFWA. this feature should push the bulk of
the precip away, but can't rule out some very light showers or
drizzle at times. MVFR cigs are expected for the most part,
likely bouncing around fuel-alternate levels with some potential
for brief excursions to low end VFR. 

General status quo for the remainder of the period, with the
next trough not arriving till outside the forecast period. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 PM EST Thursday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

UPDATE...Fisher
DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Fisher

spc.text:
SPC AC 041615

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1015 AM CST Wed Nov 04 2026

   Valid 041630Z - 051200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON
   AND EVENING OVER PARTS OF THE SOUTHEAST STATES...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and a tornado or two
   will be possible across parts of the Southeast.

   ...Southeast...
   Moderately strong cyclonic flow aloft is present over the southeast
   states today, with water vapor imagery showing a pronounced
   shortwave trough over MS/AL.  As this trough translates eastward
   today, scattered thunderstorms will affect parts of AL/GA/SC and
   east TN.  Two regimes appear to pose a risk of isolated
   strong/severe storms later today.

   The first area is along the primary cold front over eastern AL and
   western GA.  Most recent CAM solutions suggest scattered
   thunderstorms will develop along the front by mid-afternoon, with at
   least pockets of heating occurring out ahead.  A few supercells are
   possible.  Forecast soundings show weakening low-level winds and
   some veering in areas of better heating.  This may tend to reduce
   the tornado risk, but the strongest cells could be capable of
   locally damaging wind gusts.

   Another area of concern will stretch from central/northeast GA into
   upstate SC later today.  Low-level winds will remain backed and
   moderately strong in this area, leading to favorable shear profiles
   for a tornado or two in the more persistent storms.

   ..Hart/Smith.. 11/04/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 041723

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1123 AM CST Wed Nov 04 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A mid/upper trough extending from the Great Lakes to the
   central/southern Plains early Thursday will pivot eastward, becoming
   oriented from the Great Lakes to the TN Valley by early Friday. A
   belt of enhanced southwesterly midlevel flow will extend from the
   southern Plains to the Lower Great Lakes and Northeast. However,
   this stronger flow will mainly be focused behind a surface cold
   front that will slowly progress eastward across the Appalachians.
   Ahead of the front, a moist airmass will be in place, supporting
   widespread cloud cover within the warm advection regime from GA to
   southern New England. This will limit stronger destabilization, but
   scattered showers and thunderstorms are possible, though severe
   potential will remain unlikely.

   Elsewhere, a southern vorticity max will move across OK near the
   tail end of the larger-scale eastern trough. Strong cooling aloft
   will support elevated instability, with a few thunderstorms during
   the day. Late-night elevated thunderstorms may also occur over Deep
   South TX, as a cold front undercuts a moist air mass.

   ..Leitman.. 11/04/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.summary: A few strong storms are possible Friday over parts of eastern North Carolina and Virginia.
spc.text:
SPC AC 040825

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0225 AM CST Wed Nov 04 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few strong storms are possible Friday over parts of eastern North
   Carolina and Virginia.

   ...Discussion...
   On Friday, the southern lobe of the eastern trough will move rapidly
   east from the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys and into the Mid Atlantic
   by afternoon, with strong cooling aloft and increasing midlevel
   winds over 60 kt. A surface trough will deepen a bit during the day
   over the eastern Carolinas and Virginia, where mid 60s F dewpoints
   will be in place.

   Early day rain and thunderstorms will be possible, which may
   mitigate destabilization somewhat. However, at least some diurnal
   surface heating may occur upstream/south, with gradual warming and
   further destabilization during the day via advection. Increasing
   large-scale lift may support renewed development along the effective
   outflow/baroclinic zone. Given increasing mean wind fields aloft and
   favorable deep-layer shear, at least isolated damaging gusts may
   occur.

   Given the ongoing early day rain and some model discrepancy as to
   effective frontal position, will defer possible low severe
   probabilities to later updates.

   ..Jewell.. 11/04/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
